Scene: a long, low, windowless Art Nouveau stone hall seen from directly above with its roof removed, lying horizontally across the whole frame: the hall floor is one long rectangle from the left edge (north end) to the right edge (south end), filling the middle band of the frame from 35 percent to 65 percent down. The floor is worn honey-coloured limestone flags about 60 cm square, slightly dished along the centre, edged along both long walls by a narrow pastel-and-gold mosaic border of flowing vine tesserae. The two long walls are continuous thick honey-limestone wall lines along the top and bottom edges of the floor; in each wall line twelve evenly spaced shallow notches, each filled flush with dark oak; one more notch in the middle of the right-hand end wall. At the lower left, just in from the left end, a wide gap in the bottom wall line opens into a dark narrow passage running down to the bottom edge of the frame. The left end wall is a solid thick wall line. On the centre line, a row of eleven small round pastel-glass lamp tops, evenly spaced along the hall, each at the centre of a round warm amber pool of light on the floor, darker between the pools. About two-thirds of the way from the left, on the centre line, a small round clear glass table top about 50 cm across with a tiny gold key on it. Against the top wall line, about 79 percent from the left, a low faded crimson curtain lies as a thin strip hugging the base of the wall between two notches. Outside the hall the rest of the frame above and below is solid dark masonry, filled to all edges.
Dream register: grand weathered Art Nouveau set after Alphonse Mucha, aged, damp, mossy and gilded, cool verdigris-teal and slate-grey ambience with aged pastel sage, lilac, dusty-rose and tarnished-gold accents.
Projection: true orthographic top-down plan view, camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground, telecentric, infinitely far directly overhead, no perspective and no parallax; no wall face, no elevation, no facade and no side of any object is visible; only the floor or ground plane, the top edges and thickness of walls and the top surfaces of objects are seen. Every wall line runs parallel to the frame edges, no line converges to a vanishing point, each wall is a strip of constant width, the same element has the same size anywhere in the frame. The image is filled edge to edge, no black background, no vignette, no border, not a model floating on a background. Soft even light, objects cast almost no shadow that would reveal their height. No people, no animals, no text, no labels, no arrows.
Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
